sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bulk Transactional Email API and Newsletter Hosting Platform

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Marshall Islands (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinctions)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: common law corporate statute modeled on the Delaware General Corporation Law, with a written Constitution and incorporated customary law elements; no civil law or Sharia components
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus, in force for RMI since 13 December 2020)
No comprehensive double taxation agreements currently in force; reliance on domestic foreign-source tax exemption

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2022 (AMLCFTA 2022) as amended, with FIU subsidiary directives; Business Corporations Act of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, MIRC Title 36; RMI Economic Substance Regulations 2020; Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961 in force for RMI since 14 December 1992. Registered agents act as obliged entities and must maintain a confidential Beneficial Ownership Register filed with the Registrar of Corporations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Excerpt of charter and Certificate of Good Standing of each corporate UBO/shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating company registry of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the document's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO and ownership structure declaration, including full control-chain diagram
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Individual UBOs and directors, executed before a notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille in the UBO's country of residence; consular legalization if origin state is not a Hague contracting party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the country of citizenship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille; full consular legalization via RMI embassy/consulate if the issuing state is not a Hague party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (bank statement or utility bill not older than three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution or utility provider of UBO/director

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming financial standing and AML posture
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: UBO's or proposed entity's issuing bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of a bank officer; apostille recommended per prevailing registered-agent practice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the licensed RMI registered agent

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory adverse-media and sanctions screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against OFAC SDN, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated List, UK HMT Consolidated List, and RMI domestic designations. PEP categorization occurs at onboarding and is refreshed on a rolling basis; enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs, their relatives, and close associates. Notwithstanding the assigned Low_Risk_Standard tier for email-infrastructure SaaS, screening is non-discretionary. All results are documented in the registered agent's compliance file for not less than five years following termination of the business relationship, consistent with AMLCFTA 2022 and FATF Recommendations 10-12.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RMI Registrar of Corporations - Business Registry; filings are accepted exclusively through licensed RMI registered agents via the Association of Registered Agents portal; no direct retail filing portal exists for foreign applicants.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the official corporate language; names must use Latin/Roman script only; permitted characters are A-Z, Arabic numerals, hyphen, and period; CJK or other non-Latin transliteration is neither required nor accepted; mandatory corporate suffix: Incorporated, Corporation, Limited, Inc., Corp., or Ltd.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank - requires RMI Banking Commission license
Trust / Trustee - requires trust business license
Insurance / Assurance / Reinsurance - requires insurance regulator license
Finance / Financial / Securities / Fund - requires financial services authorization
University / College / Medical / Pharmacy - professional licensing requirements
Government / State / National / Federal / Authority / Republic - implies sovereign connection
Marshall Islands / Marshal / RMI - restricted to prevent official misrepresentation
Cooperative / Chamber of Commerce / Charity - special approval required
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may: (1) resubmit with a corrected name through the licensed registered agent without penalty; (2) file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of Corporations within 14 days of rejection, stating distinctiveness and compliance with BCA naming criteria; (3) if the Registrar affirms the rejection, appeal to the High Court of the Marshall Islands within 30 days. A validly reserved name may be extended twice for 30 days each upon payment of the statutory extension fee, but must be used in incorporation before final expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted. The entity is a non-resident Business Corporation with no local employees or physical operations; a licensed registered agent must maintain the statutory registered office in Majuro. Email-infrastructure SaaS is not a relevant activity under the RMI Economic Substance Regulations 2020, so no local payroll, asset, or physical-presence test is imposed for this profile.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated below 5% annual probability for a standard low-risk email-SaaS non-resident BC. Unannounced inspections are directed primarily at licensed banking, insurance, trust, and IP-holding or finance-lease entities; the registered agent must remain responsive to Registrar inquiries and maintain UBO records on file.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and clearance filing fee (one primary name, including administrative availability search)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (paid via licensed registered agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Business Corporations Act, MIRC Title 36

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Optional secondary name reservation in case of primary-name rejection
Business Corporation incorporation and charter filing fee (no minimum capital requirement)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee benchmark range USD 120-180

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and registered office annual retainer, first year, non-resident BC
Compulsory customer due diligence, UBO verification, PEP and OFAC/UN sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered agent as obliged entity under AMLCFTA 2022
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; statutory CDD obligation under AMLCFTA 2022

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Hague Apostille processing of UBO, passport, address, and POA evidence (up to four originals)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and competent apostille authority in country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing governmental and notarial certification tariffs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified passport copy and bank reference letter procurement
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Issuing bank, notary, and certification service provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: International courier of executed originals to RMI registered agent
Legal drafting review: articles of incorporation, by-laws, board consent, and power of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Outside counsel / licensed corporate service provider

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act (BCA), Title 51, Chapter 2, Marshall Islands Revised Code, as amended — §§ 101 (incorporators), 102 (contents of articles of incorporation), 106 (commencement of corporate existence), 108 (organization meeting of directors), 131-132 (registered office and registered agent), 142 (by-laws), and the Registrar of Corporations Fee Schedule.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro (filings effected through a licensed Marshall Islands registered agent).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (corporate charter), BCA § 102, filed in original with the Registrar of Corporations.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum authorized or paid-up capital applies to an MH_BC non-resident Business Corporation; the Articles state the authorized shares (here 5,000,000 shares, par US$0.01). No escrow or capital-verification deposit is required. The founding subscriber pays the board-subscribed par value directly into the corporate treasury, and the Registrar's capital-band fee is calculated from total authorized capital at filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, as the First Board Resolution of the Corporation, that the subscription and issuance of five million (5,000,000) shares of common stock, par value US$0.01 per share, to the founding shareholder at par, are ratified and approved. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office at the Trust Company Complex, Ajeltake Road, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the appointment of the registered agent, are adopted as the statutory address for service of process. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following officers are appointed: President and Chief Executive Officer, Secretary, and Treasurer. RESOLVED FURTHER, that management may open bank and payment-processing accounts, adopt the corporate seal, and execute email infrastructure vendor agreements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Registered Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands (via a licensed registered agent admitted to the Association of Registered Agents).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Marshall Islands licensed registered agent, and instruct the agent to file a name availability request with the Registrar for the proposed corporate name ending in 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or an accepted abbreviation. Document the ISIC 6201 business purpose (bulk transactional email API and newsletter hosting). Secure the name for a statutory reservation period.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and two alternates
Concise business purpose description (ISIC 6201 / bulk transactional email API, newsletter hosting platform)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for causing confusion with an existing or reserved name, resubmit a remedial name availability application with alternates; the reservation is renewable on payment of the renewal fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator instructed by the corporate services provider; document acknowledged before a notary public or the Registrar's deputy.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation under BCA § 102 containing six articles: (1) corporate name; (2) business purpose; (3) authorized capital — 5,000,000 common shares, par value US$0.01; (4) registered office and registered agent in Majuro; (5) number of directors; and (6) name and address of the incorporator. Execute the instrument, and have the registered agent countersign its acceptance of appointment.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copy of the incorporator and ultimate beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A returning of the instrument as deficient is cured by executing an amended Articles and re-filing within ten registry days, preserving the original filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Payment of Government Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands — submission through the registered agent's secure filing channel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Articles with the Registrar together with the state filing fee (US$350 base registration fee plus the capital-band fee computed on authorized shares). Pay by bank transfer in favor of the Registrar through the agent's disbursement account. The Registrar examines name, purpose, capital, and agent sufficiency, records the filing, and certifies the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation with Registrar fee schedule transmittal
Remittance advice evidencing clearance of state fees
Registered agent certificate confirming office and agent acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A Registry Defect Query is cured by the registered agent filing a certificate of correction within 21 days; the corrected filing takes effect as of the original submission date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations register; corporate services file maintained by the registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon certification, verify the legal name, date of incorporation, registered office and agent, authorized capitalization, and director count on the Certificate of Incorporation. Obtain a Certificate of Good Standing as a non-resident exempt corporation, confirming that no local tax registration or industrial permit is attached to the entity.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Material errors in the certificate are cured by a written application for a Registrar-issued corrected certificate; no re-filing fee applies for registry scrivener errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and Adoption of the First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors acting by unanimous written consent (mirroring BCA organizational-meeting provisions) or at a recorded organizational meeting.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, adopt the First Board Resolution approving the founding shareholder share subscription, fixing the registered office and agent, appointing the President/CEO, Secretary, and Treasurer, opening banking and payment-processing relationships, and ratifying the corporate seal. Approve the By-Laws governing boards and indemnification, and issue the physical share certificate to the subscriber.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution (unanimous written consent or meeting minutes)
Share certificate and stock transfer ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A missed statutory organizational meeting is cured by a unanimous written consent executed by all directors; corporately ratified acts are validated retroactively in the consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Compliance Dossier and Annual Franchise Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent and Registrar of Corporations annual corporate renewal desk.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Close the formation file by assembling the corporate book: BCA charter, good standing certificate, board resolution, by-laws, share ledger, and registered agent agreement. Register the entity for the annual corporate renewal cycle, confirming the non-resident tax-exempt status requires no domestic income tax filing; pay the annual franchise maintenance fee through the agent.
required_dossiers: Annual government maintenance fee remittance receipt
Entity formation binder including all constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A lapse in annual maintenance is cured within the statutory grace period by paying arrears and a reinstatement fee; the Registrar issues a Certificate of Reinstatement before the corporation continues transacting.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Resources and Development, Republic of the Marshall Islands (residual foreign investment and trade licence jurisdiction — not engaged for a non-resident digital services corporation).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable. The MH_BC is a non-resident corporation operating a serverless bulk transactional email API and newsletter hosting platform with no physical premises, employees, or manufacturing in the RMI; it requires no Foreign Investment Business Licence, trade licence, or industrial operating permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Republic of the Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority (RMIEPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempted Development — Class IV digital communications service under the RMI EIA Regulations: no EIA Report, environmental registration, or preliminary environmental review is required for the cloud-hosted email infrastructure platform.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No physical discharge streams exist. Should an office space be leased later, wastewater must meet RMIEPA water quality effluent standards; regulated e-waste must be exported under the RMI Solid Waste Management Regulations; any emergency generator must comply with RMIEPA ambient air standards (no fuel-burning plant within 50 metres of a sensitive receptor); no VOC or hazardous air pollutant thresholds are triggered by the software operation itself.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not engaged for remote cloud operations. In the event of a future RMI dry-desk presence: fire safety certification from the Majuro Fire Department, structural load inspection under the RMI building code, and an Occupational Safety and Health workplace clearance must be obtained before occupancy; no clearance is required for the current virtualized email infrastructure.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Revenue and Taxation Division (RTD), Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI), Majuro; operating under the Income Tax Act 1989, the Business License Act 2011, and the RMI Customs Tariff provisions. For non-resident business corporations, the functionally relevant registry is the Office of the Registrar of Marshall Islands Corporations (ROMIC) — official portal: https://www.romic.org — which administers incorporation, annual franchise filings, and Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC) declarations. No separate national taxpayer web portal exists for tax-exempt offshore entities; statutory texts are published via the Pacific Islands Legal Information Institute (http://www.paclii.org).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Appoint a licensed RMI registered agent (mandatory under the Business Corporations Act 1990). Step 2: Reserve the proposed corporate name with ROMIC. Step 3: File Articles of Incorporation, including the NRDC declaration, with the registered agent; ROMIC issues the Certificate of Incorporation and a permanent Registry Number. Step 4: Pay the one-time incorporation fee based on authorized share capital and receive the registered-agent file references. Step 5: File the annual franchise/filing report and pay the fixed annual government fee to ROMIC each anniversary; no local tax return is required because the entity is tax-exempt. Step 6: Because a pure NRDC is wholly exempt from income tax, no General TIN or VAT ID is issued or required; the ROMIC Registry Number and the NRDC Certificate operate as the entity's statutory tax identifiers. Step 7 (optional but prudent): Apply to the U.S. IRS for an EIN via Form SS-4 as a foreign entity for FATCA documentation, Stripe Billing onboarding, and U.S. information reporting. Step 8: The registered agent must maintain current beneficial-ownership records under RMI beneficial-ownership and AML/CFT rules for production to the Registrar on demand.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — A Marshall Islands Business Corporation (BC) is a juridical person with limited liability. A Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC) conducting all business outside the RMI and deriving no RMI-source income is statutorily exempt from national income tax, capital gains tax, and withholding tax on dividends, interest, or royalties paid to non-residents. Entity-level taxation is not triggered; the exemption is a statutory status, not a pass-through election. No RMI payroll or social-security contributions apply absent locally employed individuals in the RMI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: 1) NRDC status election under the Non-Resident Domestic Corporations Act 1985: the incorporator files a certificate/declaration with ROMIC, through the registered agent, certifying that all business will be conducted outside the RMI; this election is recorded on the corporate register. 2) Domestic check-the-box election: none, because no income tax is imposed on a compliant NRDC. 3) U.S. federal classification: an entity formed under Marshall Islands law is not a per se corporation under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-2(b)(8)(i); therefore, U.S. owners may file IRS Form 8832 to elect corporate, partnership, or disregarded-entity classification for U.S. tax purposes. 4) Hybrid mismatch rules: the RMI has no domestic hybrid-mismatch legislation; any BEPS Action 2 consequences are determined exclusively under the shareholder's home jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT / GST / Sales and Use Tax in the RMI. The only indirect-style levy is customs import duty on physical goods entering the Islands. Cross-border email-API subscriptions, newsletter-hosting fees, and SaaS infrastructure revenues are outside the scope of any RMI indirect tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — the RMI has no indirect tax registration regime, no services-tax threshold, and no digital-services tax. An NRDC supplying email and newsletter infrastructure to foreign clients has no RMI indirect tax registration obligation regardless of turnover. Customs import duty arises only per shipment on physical goods and is not connected to any economic turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. The RMI has not introduced real-time fiscal clearance, SAF-T, B2B/B2C e-invoicing, QR-code digital stamping, or API-connected invoice clearance. The entity must only maintain ordinary commercial records, invoices, and payment receipts in accordance with general record-keeping rules; Stripe Billing transaction records satisfy standard evidentiary practice for the NRDC's registered-agent file.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable — the RMI does not operate a VAT/GST system, so there is no export zero-rating mechanism and no refund procedure to substantiate. Cross-border email-API and newsletter-hosting services rendered by an NRDC are foreign-source and wholly outside the RMI tax net. The RMI has no exchange-control regime and uses the U.S. Dollar, so no foreign-exchange repatriation deadline is imposed (effective deadline in days: 0).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: N/A — pure digital services; no customs entry or export declaration is required for email/API/software deliverables
Export service contract / master subscription agreement evidencing offshore supply and a foreign counterparty
Commercial invoice generated by the billing system (e.g., Stripe Billing)
Certificate of good standing / NRDC certificate from ROMIC for banking and corporate-record substantiation
If physical hardware is ever exported: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading/Airway Bill, and customs permit — required only in that goods-based scenario
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No zero-rating or refund regime exists, so there is no export-fraud refund clawback mechanism. The substantive compliance risks are: (a) misrepresenting NRDC status by carrying on business within the RMI — the Revenue and Taxation Division or Business License Office may revoke the exemption, retrospectively reassess RMI-source income at the statutory corporate income tax rate, apply interest and civil fraud penalties at statutory rates, and pursue criminal fines and imprisonment for wilful false declarations; (b) failure to file the annual franchise report — ROMIC may dissolve the BC, and reinstatement requires payment of all delinquent annual fees plus penalties; (c) AML/CFT or beneficial-ownership non-compliance by the registered agent attracts regulatory fines and possible disqualification; and (d) U.S. informational penalties (Forms 5472, 8832, and FATCA) attach to the U.S. owner, not to the RMI entity.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Office of the Banking Commissioner, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands (no domestic central bank; U.S. dollar is the sole legal tender issued by the U.S. Federal Reserve)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Marshall Islands operates as a de facto dollarized economy with full and unrestricted convertibility on both capital and current account transactions. There are no exchange controls, no advance approvals for foreign investment remittances, and profit repatriation and capital liquidation proceeds may be freely wired abroad without quantitative limits or licensing requirements. The only practical compliance layer is standard anti-money laundering (AML) verification of beneficial ownership and end-use declarations by the receiving bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the state or to convert any portion of export receipts into local currency. Because the U.S. dollar is the domestic currency, all export earnings remain in the same currency, and no mandatory conversion ratio or time-bound repatriation rule applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD multicurrency equivalent) as primary treasury account; Capital Escrow Account may be opened for committed capital injection verification

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam (RMI branch) – under RMI banking license
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account for payment routing and contingency liquidity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. The Marshall Islands has no fintech e-money institution (EMI) licensing framework that would grant a standalone offshore EMI portal for corporate treasury operations. Offshore digital banks or unlicensed virtual asset service providers are not accepted by RMI commercial banks as viable settlement counterparties for primary liquidity clearing. A non-resident entity may use regulated U.S.-chartered fintech banks (e.g., a chartered digital bank) as a supplementary clearing rail, but such arrangements are not a substitute for a licensed RMI domestic bank account and do not replace the AML/beneficial ownership verification required by BOMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the Bank of Marshall Islands, corporate directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) are not required to be physically present on-island for every transaction, but a physical identity verification or a remotely notarized and apostilled video interview is mandatory during initial onboarding. At least one signatory (director or authorized officer) must complete a live video interview with a compliance officer. Non-resident directors may satisfy the presence requirement by attending through a remote video link, provided that all passport, proof of address, corporate charter, and apostilled resolution documents are authenticated by a licensed RMI registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdiction diversification with high-risk or sanctioned counterparty exposure (e.g., non-cooperative tax havens)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate chart and ultimate beneficial ownership ledger mapped to head-office jurisdiction; source-of-funds declaration with bank statements evidencing clean prior transactions; OFAC, EU, and UN sanctions screening reports for all counterparties; board resolution authorizing the account; apostilled certificate of good standing from the RMI Registrar.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.documentation_bundle_requirements: Submit an organizational chart with each entity's FATCA/GIIN, CRS registration, or tax residence confirmation; certified copy of the operating agreement; bank reference from a major U.S. or treaty bank; and an AML compliance manual demonstrating adequate transaction monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Subscription-based email/API platform with high transaction volume and cross-border card clearing (Stripe/Card)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan explaining the software-as-a-service model, the non-anonymous nature of the platform, data privacy policy, and payment processor KYC standards; sample customer onboarding language showing the platform does not facilitate money laundering or terrorist financing; proof of PCI DSS compliance; clear merchant-of-record and know-your-customer (KYC) procedures of Stripe and acquiring banks; and a projected transaction flow diagram.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.documentation_bundle_requirements: Provide merchant account / processor records, historical settlement statements, and the underlying email newsletter distribution agreements that prove the transactional purpose is legitimate digital infrastructure services under ISIC 6201. Include a third-party compliance audit letter if necessary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No physical office or staff in the Marshall Islands (non-resident shell activity perception)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered agent contract with a licensed RMI corporate service provider; lease or service agreement for a registered office at the agent's premises; appointment of a local director or secretary where deemed necessary; evidence of economic substance through global employees, servers, and intellectual property ownership; and board minutes documenting centralized treasury decisions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.documentation_bundle_requirements: Provide the RMI Business Corporations Act compliance certificate, latest annual report filing, beneficial ownership register, and a sworn statement that the entity does not engage in any prohibited activities. Include tax residency or tax exemption confirmation from the RMI competent authority.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection is executed via SWIFT MT103 wire from the investor's bank to the RMI domestic bank account. The wire must carry a standard capital purpose code, generally 'S1301' (direct inward investment) or an equivalent corporate service description recognized by the receiving bank, accompanied by the definitive share subscription agreement, board resolution, and investor's source-of-wealth questionnaire. The RMI bank will verify the beneficial owner through the UBO register and screen all parties against OFAC and UN sanctions lists. The funds are then credited to the Operational Account and may be held in a segregated Capital Escrow Account until the legal capital deployment is evidenced by contracts or tax filings.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and operational disbursements are cleared through the same USD SWIFT infrastructure. Standard settlement rails include: (1) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border supplier payments and SaaS licensing fees with corresponding purpose codes; (2) commercial letters of credit (documentary LC) for any physical goods movement, drawn on a U.S. correspondent bank; and (3) intra-group clearing via SWIFT MT101/MT103 between RMI entity and related operating subsidiaries. For cards and merchant acquiring, the platform may route to Stripe as the principal payment gateway; Stripe then settles in USD through U.S. ACH/Fedwire to the RMI operating bank. No local clearing house is involved because the domestic currency is USD.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: No onshore FX market exists in the Marshall Islands; since the USD is legal tender, no FX hedge is required for operations denominated in USD.

Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts executed through a non-resident international bank are permissible for hedging nominal exposure to non-USD customer refunds or vendor payments, but these are not settled in the RMI and do not require local regulatory approval.

Cross-currency swaps are permissible solely for treasury risk management when the counterparty is an OECD-licensed bank; documentation must evidence business purpose and will be scrutinized by the RMI bank's AML unit.
Spot USD exchange through the domestic bank's correspondent network is permitted for conversion of incidental foreign currency receipts, but no leveraged or speculative FX transactions are allowed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Report (Annual Return) - Business Corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Registrar, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the month in which the incorporation anniversary occurs (e.g., incorporation 15 March -> file by 31 March annually)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: US$200 late penalty if filed within the first month after the due date; continued non-filing beyond one year permits the Registrar to cancel or revoke the certificate of incorporation (administrative strike-off)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC) Annual Status Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations (NRDC Registry), Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same anniversary-month window as the Annual Corporate Report; declaration effective as of the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Forfeiture of non-resident domesticated status; reclassification as a fully domestic corporation; loss of tax-exempt / zero-tax treatment; monetary penalty and potential administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Filing with the Marshall Islands Registered Agent (kept on file; subject to inspection by the Marshall Islands Banking Commissioner / FIU)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual UBO confirmation to be executed at the annual report anniversary; immediate notice to the registered agent upon any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under the Beneficial Ownership Regulations; registered agent may be obligated to file a compliance report with authorities; sustained non-compliance can trigger strike-off and director disqualification

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit required for an unlisted, non-resident Business Corporation under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act. A mandatory audit is triggered only if (a) the articles or bylaws expressly require an audit, (b) shareholders holding at least 10% of the voting shares demand an audit in accordance with the BCA, or (c) the entity licenses or operates a regulated activity. Bulk transactional email / newsletter SaaS infrastructure entity: no compulsory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or US GAAP voluntarily adopted; the BCA mandates that books and records accurately reflect transactions and the financial condition of the corporation, but prescribes no single accounting framework for unlisted non-resident BCs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must maintain and annually confirm the beneficial ownership register. All direct or indirect share transfers must be reconciled with the Register of Members and the UBO register before the annual confirmation is executed. The corporation must certify the UBO schedule as of the anniversary date and notify the registered agent within a reasonable period (typically no later than 21 days) of any new share transfer or change in control, regardless of the annual cycle.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (held by Registered Agent)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 (statutorily exempt); voluntary certified audit or financial statement compilation typically USD 4,000 - 8,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for a non-resident Business Corporation (BC) deriving no income from sources within the Republic of the Marshall Islands; the 3% Gross Revenue Tax under the Gross Revenue Tax Act 1989 applies only to entities licensed to carry on business within the RMI and does not attach to foreign-source subscription, API, or newsletter infrastructure revenue.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Non-resident Domestic Corporation exemption under the Business Corporations Act and Income Tax Act 1989: zero RMI corporate income tax, zero gross revenue tax, zero capital gains tax, and zero withholding tax on dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents; no capital duty, no annual net-worth tax, and no ATAD-style top-up tax for entities outside the scope of the Economic Substance (Amendment) Act 2019.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form R-1 (Corporation Income Tax Return) filed electronically via the RMI Revenue and Taxation (RETAX) online portal; the operative annual compliance instrument for a non-resident BC is the Annual Report and Government Maintenance Fee filing with the Registrar of Corporations, submitted through the licensed Registered Agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form R-1: due on or before the last day of the third month following the close of the tax year, which defaults to the calendar year unless the BC elects a different fiscal year. Registry Annual Report and Government Maintenance Fee: due on the statutory renewal anniversary of the entity, processed by the Registered Agent; payment continuity is required to preserve corporate existence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 — Gross Revenue from RMI Sources
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross revenue derived from sources within the Marshall Islands, including revenue from RMI resident counterparties, local agency sales, and services physically performed in the RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0.00 where all API subscription, email newsletter hosting, and infrastructure service revenue is sourced outside the RMI; retain source documentation, IP geolocation logs, and contracting evidence in working papers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 — Allowable Deductions / Cost of Goods Sold
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses allowable against gross revenue for a licensee electing the net-income route under the Income Tax Act 1989.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Leave nil or enter N/A; deductions are inapplicable where the entity is outside the RMI tax net and reports zero RMI-source gross revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Presumptive tax liability imposed on the gross revenue of an entity licensed to conduct business within the RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report 0.00; no General Business License is required for a non-resident BC that has no RMI place of business, employees, or dependent agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 — Net Income / Alternative Income Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax exposure under Income Tax Act 1989 on net RMI-source income where the BC has a permanent establishment or dependent agent in the RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0.00 and attach a non-resident position statement confirming: no PE, no dependent agent, no RMI board meetings, and no RMI-source sales activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule A — Non-Resident Status Declaration and Beneficial Ownership Statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Self-declaration of non-resident domestic corporation status, UBO identification, and confirmation of the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark 'Non-Resident Domestic Corporation,' disclose the ultimate beneficial owner to the agent, and cite the Registered Agent certificate number; keep the beneficial ownership register current but non-public.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form R-1: statutory penalty of 5% per month or fraction thereof on the unpaid tax, capped at 25%, plus statutory interest at 1.5% per month. Late filing of the Registry Annual Report or non-payment of the Government Maintenance Fee: late penalty equal to the annual fee amount, risk of administrative penalty, and automatic dissolution after two consecutive years of non-payment; reinstatement requires payment of all back fees, penalties, a reinstatement fee, and a director certification of continued solvency.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — the Marshall Islands imposes no withholding tax on dividends declared or paid by a Business Corporation to shareholders, whether resident or non-resident; dividends are outside RMI source-based taxation under the Income Tax Act 1989.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The RMI maintains no comprehensive double taxation agreements (DTA network: nil), so no treaty-relief protocol, Tax Residency Certificate issuance, or Limitation on Benefits filing exists. Where a foreign payer bank or revenue authority requires proof of entitlement to an exemption or reduced rate, the shareholder obtains: (i) Certificate of Good Standing from the RMI Registrar; (ii) Certificate of Non-Residence / Tax Domicile from the RMI Revenue and Taxation Department; and (iii) the relevant domestic foreign-tax-credit or exemption form in the shareholder's residence jurisdiction, e.g., IRS Form 1118 for a US corporate shareholder; the RMI certificate documents no RMI-source income rather than claiming treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory RMI rates: 0% on interest and 0% on royalties paid to non-residents, provided the income is not attributable to an RMI permanent establishment or RMI-source business activity; the applicable treaty rate is N/A because no DTA is in force. Payments for the email newsletter platform's software IP, brand, and hosting infrastructure are therefore repatriation-tested only in the recipient's residence jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory transfer pricing regime, Local File, Master File, or related-party transaction threshold exists under RMI law. Best-practice governance threshold: maintain contemporaneous arm's-length documentation and a benchmark study whenever annual cross-border related-party transactions, including group software licensing, intercompany API service fees, shared hosting costs, or co-marketing arrangements, exceed USD 500,000; a master-file quality group overview and per-entity local file should be retained to support foreign tax authority challenges, ESR substance records, and bank KYC reviews.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance (Amendment) Act 2019 applies to non-resident domestic companies and foreign-resident entities carrying on a 'relevant activity': banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, financing and leasing, headquarters, distribution and service centers, or intellectual property (IP) holding. A standalone email-newsletter infrastructure SaaS platform selling services to third-party non-residents is not a statutorily relevant activity unless (i) it derives royalty-type income from licensed IP held for related parties, or (ii) it operates as a group distribution or service center. If the platform is restructured as an IP-holding vehicle, the RMI entity must satisfy a proportionate economic substance test: in-RMI board meetings, physical premises, qualified employees, adequate expenditure, and an annual substance filing. As the EU currently maintains the RMI on Annex II of the non-cooperative jurisdictions list, continued monitoring of substance enforcement is required, and the operating substance of the group is anchored in the parent jurisdiction (e.g., United States) to avoid adverse shell-entity determinations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a false zero tax return, understating RMI-source revenue, or claiming the non-resident exemption while maintaining a dependent agent, an RMI office, or local newsletter subscription sales into the RMI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty equal to 100% of the understated tax plus statutory interest at 1.5% per month; criminal fine up to USD 10,000 per offense and imprisonment up to two years under the Income Tax Act 1989 and Gross Revenue Tax Act 1989.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or direct the suppression of RMI-source revenue are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt; criminal convictions carry travel bans, extradition exposure, and automatic disqualification as directors in regulated jurisdictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Missing Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a pure mailbox entity with no contracts, accounting records, board minutes, office, bank account, or payment processing relationship, while relying on the zero-tax regime; attempting to use the RMI BC directly as merchant of record with Stripe or other major card acquirers, which do not onboard Marshall Islands entities; failing to align with EU/OECD substance expectations while the RMI sits on the EU Annex II grey list.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative dissolution after two consecutive years of unpaid registry fees; voiding of contracts entered after dissolution; deboarding or refusal by payment service providers, account freezes, and US FATCA / CFC look-through treatment causing inclusion of the entity's income in the US owner's taxable base; adverse CFC and GILTI determinations eliminate the zero-tax benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who procure contracts after dissolution are personally liable for all resulting obligations; under the doctrine of sham subordination, the corporate veil is pierced in foreign prosecutions, exposing directors to civil restitution to investors and creditors, travel bans, and imprisonment of up to ten years for aggravated fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to disclose ultimate beneficial ownership to the registered agent, filing a false beneficial ownership register, or routing newsletter subscription payments derived from sanctioned, high-risk, or unexplained-source customers to obscure the origin of funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering under the RMI Criminal Code: fines, forfeiture of merchant proceeds, imprisonment up to ten years, cancellation of the registered agent license, and potential FATF consequence listing of the entity; the RMI's non-cooperative jurisdiction status amplifies bank de-risking and reputational sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced for fraud, sham, or nominee misuse: directors face civil restitution to defrauded parties, personal asset freezing, travel bans, and imprisonment up to ten years; nominee directors bear equal criminal liability and cannot invoke the corporate shield as a defense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Cross-Border Tax Mischaracterization and US CFC Exposure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mischaracterizing the RMI BC as a zero-tax operating company in the United States or the EU without a documented upstream structure: e.g., a US person directly owning the RMI BC while the RMI BC owns a disregarded US LLC that operates the newsletter platform, creating US permanent establishment, Subpart F, and GILTI inclusions, and exposing US dividend, interest, or royalty flows to 30% withholding because no US-RMI income tax treaty exists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: US: GILTI inclusion at an effective 10.5% US corporate rate (21% statutory rate after the 50% deduction) on the pro-rata share of tested income with no foreign tax credits where the RMI entity paid zero foreign tax; Form 5471 late-filing penalties of USD 10,000 per form per year, up to USD 60,000; EU: CFC rules and ATAD3 shell-entity presumptions render the structure non-transparent and deny cross-border deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The US person shareholder-director faces accuracy-related penalties of 20% for noncompliance and 40% for gross valuation misstatements; repeated violations trigger felony tax charges, civil restitution to the IRS, and travel restrictions; deliberate use of the RMI shell to conceal the US owner constitutes tax evasion subject to a six-year limitations period and indictment risk.
